title: ₹500 Ki Beer Pub Mein: Bar Owner Ko Kitna Bachta Hai?
description: Reasoning: our wine-shop reel is already covered, so this is the natural next step. Pubs are an aspirational business for young men, and the licence cost and markup are public, so the numbers are researchable. The 'why so expensive' question is something every viewer has asked.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: PUB / BAR UNIT ECONOMICS IN INDIA
Prepared 16 Nov 2026. Figures are the latest I could find. Many are indicative and vary by state and city. I flag where a source is weak or old.

**BIGGEST GAP, READ FIRST**
- I found no source that splits a ₹500 pub beer into liquor cost, tax, rent, staff and owner profit. The ₹500 breakdown has to be built from the pieces below, and each piece is labelled as a range or an estimate by its source.
- No Indian source gave a pub-specific break-even time. I found no India-specific figures for what bar owners take home, only generic restaurant and bar benchmarks.
- Aggregator licence-fee sites disagree wildly. For example, one says FL-3 fees run from ₹2 lakh in Karnataka to ₹50 lakh in Delhi [https://www.incorpx.io/guide/how-to-get-liquor-license-india]. Another says ₹3 lakh (Rajasthan) to ₹50 lakh (Karnataka) [https://www.incorpx.io/blog/liquor-license-india-types-cost-application]. Treat those as unreliable. The official Delhi numbers are below.

**1. THE PRICE GAP: WINE SHOP VS PUB (Bengaluru example)**
- Hook check: this source lists a Kingfisher 650ml at ₹170–200 at a licensed wine shop, ₹230–300 at a casual pub or restaurant, and ₹380–520 at a premium bar or lounge [https://mostnext.com/beer-price-in-bangalore/]. It is a blog, not official data, so call it "typical" and not exact.
- A ₹180 wine-shop vs ₹500 pub beer contrast is therefore plausible only at the premium-bar end.
- Microbrewery pints: ₹350–₹750 for a pint [https://mostnext.com/beer-price-in-bangalore/]. A separate Bengaluru guide says ₹200–400 per pint [https://liquorr.xyz/liquor/liquor-price-bangalore-2026]. The two sources disagree, so don't state one number as fact.
- Karnataka changed beer pricing in 2026. A blog says a new Alcohol-in-Beverage excise system took effect on May 11, 2026, and several mild and lager beers saw substantial MRP reductions [https://gyaanvibes.wordpress.com/2026/05/02/beer-price-in-bangalore-latest-rate-list-2026/]. This is a low-reliability source. Check before using the ₹180 figure for Bengaluru.

**2. WHERE THE WINE-SHOP MRP GOES (tax burden)**
- Carlsberg's Oct 2025 investor deck covers 8 Indian states with beer at ₹130–200. State government taxes are 55–65% of the consumer price. Trade margin is 9–28%. [https://www.carlsberggroup.com/media/xkfle4xy/10-carlsberg-cmd-1-oct-2025_deep-dive-india.pdf]
- The same deck says 62% of volumes are government-controlled, 24% auction-based and 14% free trade [https://www.carlsberggroup.com/media/xkfle4xy/10-carlsberg-cmd-1-oct-2025_deep-dive-india.pdf].
- Another source says state taxes account for 50% to 75% of a bottle's retail MRP [https://gstmunshi.com/blog/taxes-on-liquor-by-state-in-india]. Alcohol sits outside GST and is taxed by states.
- Maharashtra: combined excise and VAT can exceed 60% of the retail price for IMFL, and beer carries roughly 35–45% of MRP in tax [https://ndsavlaa.com/vat-on-liquor/]. It is a CA-firm blog, so treat it as indicative.
- One state-by-state list gives different effective burdens: Delhi ~25% of MRP, Maharashtra ~45% and UP ~69% [https://www.likar.app/liquor-price-list]. The methods differ, so don't compare them directly with Carlsberg's figures.
- Karnataka 2023: beer excise duty was raised from 175% to 185%. One-third of a beer bottle's price goes to the government. [https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Fkarnataka%2Fkarnataka-budget-2023-liquor-prices-to-go-up-by-20-beer-10-1234736.html]
- Wine-shop owner's cut: low single-digit to low-teens percent of MRP, set by the state, with beer at the bottom and premium spirits and wine at the top [https://okcredit.in/blog/is-a-beer-liquor-shop-a-profitable-business-in-india/]. No state publishes a clean 2026 percentage.
- Old Maharashtra data (about 2013, dated): IMFL retail margin fell from 16–17% to about 12%, and beer from 20–22% to 15% [https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-excise-department-cracks-down-on-liquor-shops-for-overcharging-customers-1930962].
- So the wine-shop owner keeps only a thin slice of ₹180. The rest is mostly brewer cost plus tax.
